instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.72(A) requires each legislative agent and employer to file an initial registration statement with the joint legislative ethics committee within ten days following an engagement.

Section 101.72(F) provides that the registration card and registration are valid from issuance until the next December 31 of an even-numbered year, meaning registrations renew every two years (biennially).

Section 101.72(G) requires a person notified of a deficiency to file an amended registration statement not later than fifteen days after receiving the notice; otherwise general changes are reflected in the next periodic updated registration statement under (D)(1).
Section 101.72(A) requires the initial registration statement to be filed within ten days following an engagement of a legislative agent.

Section 101.72(A) requires each legislative agent AND employer to file registration statements, and (C) requires a separate initial and updated registration statement for each engagement when an agent has multiple employers.

Section 101.72(A) enumerates the required contents of the initial registration statement (name, business address, occupation, employer info, description of legislation) and does not require a photograph.

Section 121.60(H) excludes from "executive agency lobbyist" any elected/appointed officer or employee of a federal/state agency, college, university, or political subdivision who attempts to influence executive agency decisions in a fiduciary capacity as a representative of that entity; section 101.90(H) provides a parallel exemption for retirement system lobbyists.

Section 101.72(E) provides that an officer or employee of a state agency who actively advocates in a fiduciary capacity as a representative of that state agency need not file expenditure statements under section 101.73 — a partial exemption (still must register and pay the fee, but is exempt from expenditure reporting).
